A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the slope of creatine kinase MB2 concentration, MM3/MM1, and MT index showed significant relations to angiographic patency after thrombolytics, but none of the isoform marker calculations had sufficient diagnostic accuracy to be useful for clinical decisions.

creatine kinase MB2 concentrations, MM3/MM1 and MT index ratios, and MB2/MB2 ratio are useful markers for assessing patency in patients undergoing acute angiography after thrombolytics; however, the diagnostic utility of these markers in the individual patient is limited.

creatine kinase isoform markers, including MB and MM isoform concentrations, are not useful for assessing coronary patency in patients undergoing thrombolytic and angiographic therapy for acute myocardial infarction.
